explanation: Aristotle, our main source, guessed he chose water because all life needs moisture. Anaximenes later picked air, and Heraclitus fire.

claims.text: Thales of Miletus held that water is the basic substance from which everything is made.
Thales did not name fire, air or earth as the basic substance of everything.
Thales is often called the first Greek philosopher.
Aristotle, the main source for Thales' views, suggested that he chose water because nourishment and life depend on moisture.
Anaximenes held that air was the basic substance, and Heraclitus held that it was fire.
